agent.note: No agent session ran m2 to produce this evidence, and no part of the m2 protocol was executed. The transcript is the output of the packaging test, run from a shell while this release was being prepared.

invocation.working_directory: a throwaway directory holding a copy of skills/ and of tests/test_package.py

transforms.name: strip-test-duration
transforms.what: The elapsed time that unittest prints after the test count was removed from the one line that reports it, so that line ends after the test count. scripts/record_session.py makes that edit. Nothing else was changed.

output.note: scripts/record_session.py wrote the command line and, from the command's exit status, the exit status line; everything between is the packaging test's output.

invocations.model_source: the init event of the stream-json output
invocations.invocation: Use /m2 for this task. (prompt text; the agent loaded the skill with a Skill tool call for m2:m2)
invocations.fixture: A synthetic git repository holding GOAL.md, a made-up three-workstream goal (backend CSV export endpoint, frontend download button, user-guide docs), with a local bare repository as origin. GOAL.md was its only tracked file. The skill was loaded with --plugin-dir from a clone of this repository at v0.1.0.

transforms.name: truncate-tool-arguments
transforms.what: Each tool call's arguments longer than 300 characters were cut to their first 300 characters, followed by ' ...[+N chars]' giving the number cut. The prompt, statuses and the final message were not cut. Applied before the replacements.

transforms.name: replace-plugin-root
transforms.what: The absolute path of the directory the client loaded the skill from (the --plugin-dir clone for Claude Code, the fixture's .agents/skills/m2 for Codex) became /plugin. Applied first.

invocations.outcome: An agent run: the agent loaded m2:m2, read GOAL.md and the four reference documents, and answered with a table of manager artifacts citing file, section and line; it started no m2 run and changed no file. Checked after the run, its File Lease row misstates the cited Phase 2 rule, which rejects the board only when two edit-capable packets can touch the same file without a lease order.
